MRNA.about: A biotechnology company that pioneered mRNA-based vaccines and therapeutics, best known for its COVID-19 vaccine.
MRNA.performance: Moderna has been the runaway standout of the FY26 roster, up more than 400% since the season open. A recovering biotech sector and renewed enthusiasm for the company's broader mRNA pipeline beyond COVID vaccines have driven the move.

AMD.about: A semiconductor company that designs CPUs and GPUs, competing directly with Nvidia and Intel in both consumer and AI data-center chips.
AMD.performance: AMD has ridden the same AI-infrastructure buildout as the rest of the chip sector, climbing over 80% since FY26 opened. Data-center GPU demand has been the main driver of the gain.

ASML.about: A Dutch company that makes the extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines every advanced chipmaker depends on — effectively a monopoly on the equipment needed to print the smallest chips.
ASML.performance: As the single supplier of leading-edge chipmaking equipment, ASML has benefited directly from the industry-wide AI chip buildout, up over 60% since the FY26 open.

CAT.about: The world's largest manufacturer of construction and mining equipment, along with diesel and natural gas engines.
CAT.performance: Caterpillar is up more than 50% since the FY26 open, helped by strong infrastructure and data-center construction spending that has kept demand for heavy equipment elevated.

GOOGL.about: Google's parent company — search, advertising, YouTube, and Google Cloud, with a growing push into AI products like Gemini.
GOOGL.performance: Alphabet is up roughly 26% since the FY26 open, with continued strength in advertising and cloud revenue alongside investor enthusiasm for its AI investments.

EQIX.about: A real estate investment trust (REIT) that owns and operates data centers around the world, leasing space and connectivity to enterprises and cloud providers.
EQIX.performance: Equinix is up about 23% since the FY26 open. Demand for data-center capacity to support AI workloads has kept occupancy and pricing strong across its facilities.

NVDA.about: The dominant maker of GPUs used for AI training and inference, along with data-center networking hardware and software.
NVDA.performance: Nvidia is up about 20% since the FY26 open. Continued heavy capital spending on AI infrastructure by its largest customers has kept demand for its chips strong.

TDY.about: A maker of specialized instrumentation, digital imaging, and sensor systems used in aerospace, defense, and industrial applications.
TDY.performance: Teledyne is up roughly 16% since the FY26 open, tracking steady demand for its instrumentation and imaging products across defense and industrial end markets.

AMZN.about: The e-commerce giant, and through Amazon Web Services (AWS), one of the largest cloud computing providers in the world.
AMZN.performance: Amazon is up about 14% since the FY26 open, supported by steady retail margins and continued growth in AWS's cloud and AI services.

V.about: One of the world's largest payment networks, processing card transactions between banks, merchants, and consumers globally.
V.performance: Visa is up modestly, about 8%, since the FY26 open — a steady, low-volatility gain consistent with its role as a payments-volume bellwether rather than a high-growth swing stock.

BEP.about: A global renewable power operator with hydroelectric, wind, solar, and storage assets across multiple continents.
BEP.performance: Brookfield Renewable is up about 5% since the FY26 open, a modest gain reflecting steady demand for renewable power generation.

MMM.about: A diversified industrial conglomerate making everything from adhesives and abrasives to safety equipment and consumer products.
MMM.performance: 3M is roughly flat since the FY26 open, consistent with a mature industrial business without a clear single catalyst pushing it strongly in either direction this season.

FSST.about: An actively managed ESG-focused ETF from Fidelity that held a portfolio of large-cap U.S. growth stocks.
FSST.performance: Fidelity liquidated this fund on November 13, 2025, cashing shareholders out at $30.8963/share. The position is now closed — its return is essentially flat since the FY26 open, reflecting the payout value rather than ongoing price action.

COST.about: A membership-based warehouse retailer known for bulk goods, high member retention, and thin but consistent margins.
COST.performance: Costco is roughly flat, down about 1.5%, since the FY26 open — a small pullback for a stock generally viewed as a steady, defensive retail holding.

NEE.about: The largest electric utility holding company in the U.S. by market cap, and the world's largest generator of wind and solar energy.
NEE.performance: NextEra is down about 3% since the FY26 open, a modest decline typical of a large regulated utility whose stock tends to move less than the broader market.

PG.about: A consumer packaged goods giant behind brands like Tide, Gillette, Pampers, and Crest.
PG.performance: P&G is down about 3.5% since the FY26 open, a modest slide consistent with a slow-growth consumer staples business rather than any single sharp setback.

SG.about: A fast-casual restaurant chain focused on salads and healthy bowls, with a tech-forward ordering and loyalty platform.
SG.performance: Sweetgreen is down about 5.5% since the FY26 open, reflecting the ongoing pressure fast-casual restaurant chains have faced from cautious consumer spending.

MSFT.about: A software and cloud computing giant — Windows, Office, and Azure — with a major investment stake in OpenAI and a broad AI product push.
MSFT.performance: Microsoft is down about 6% since the FY26 open, a modest pullback even as the company continues investing heavily in AI infrastructure and Copilot products.

PLTR.about: A data analytics and AI software company that builds platforms for government intelligence, defense, and large enterprise customers.
PLTR.performance: Palantir is down about 8% since the FY26 open — a pullback after an extended run-up in the stock, with valuation concerns weighing on sentiment despite continued government and commercial contract wins.

CMG.about: A fast-casual restaurant chain known for build-your-own burritos and bowls, and for its emphasis on "food with integrity" sourcing.
CMG.performance: Chipotle is down about 10% since the FY26 open, reflecting slower same-store sales growth as the fast-casual dining category has cooled.

MP.about: The owner and operator of the only active rare earth mining and processing facility in the United States, at Mountain Pass, California.
MP.performance: MP Materials is down about 17% since the FY26 open. Rare earth prices and the pace of the company's domestic supply-chain buildout have been volatile, weighing on the stock.

SHOP.about: An e-commerce platform that lets businesses of any size build and run online stores, handling payments, shipping, and marketing.
SHOP.performance: Shopify is down about 17% since the FY26 open, as slowing merchant growth and a more cautious e-commerce spending environment have pressured the stock.

META.about: The parent company of Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp, with heavy ongoing investment in AI and the metaverse/Reality Labs division.
META.performance: Meta is down about 18% since the FY26 open. Heavy capital spending on AI infrastructure and Reality Labs, without a clear near-term payoff, has weighed on investor sentiment.

TSLA.about: An electric vehicle and clean energy company, also developing autonomous driving software and robotics.
TSLA.performance: Tesla is down about 22% since the FY26 open. Slowing EV delivery growth and intensifying competition have offset optimism around its autonomy and robotics ambitions.

SMCI.about: A maker of high-performance servers and storage systems built for data centers, particularly AI and cloud computing workloads.
SMCI.performance: Super Micro is down about 23% since the FY26 open. The stock has remained volatile as investors weigh strong AI server demand against margin pressure and past accounting concerns.

NOW.about: An enterprise software company whose platform automates IT, HR, and customer service workflows for large organizations.
NOW.performance: ServiceNow is down about 25% since the FY26 open, as slower enterprise software spending growth has weighed on high-multiple SaaS names broadly.

RDDT.about: A social media and discussion platform organized around topic-based communities, monetized through advertising and data-licensing deals.
RDDT.performance: Reddit is down about 30% since the FY26 open. Slowing user growth and increased competition for advertising dollars have pressured the stock after a strong post-IPO run.

FBTC.about: A spot Bitcoin exchange-traded fund from Fidelity that holds actual bitcoin, tracking the cryptocurrency's price directly.
FBTC.performance: FBTC is down about 31% since the FY26 open, tracking a sharp pullback in the price of bitcoin itself over the period.

NKE.about: The world's largest athletic footwear and apparel company, selling through both its own stores/DTC channel and wholesale retail partners.
NKE.performance: Nike is down about 44% since the FY26 open. A prolonged turnaround effort, weaker wholesale demand, and market-share losses to newer athletic brands have all weighed heavily on the stock.

KTOS.about: A defense technology company specializing in unmanned aerial systems (drones), satellite communications, and missile defense systems.
KTOS.performance: Kratos is down about 47% since the FY26 open, a sharp pullback after a period of elevated valuations tied to defense-spending optimism that has since cooled.

ZS.about: A cloud security company providing "zero trust" network security services that route enterprise internet traffic through its cloud platform.
ZS.performance: Zscaler is down about 48% since the FY26 open, as slowing growth and heightened competition in the cloud security space have hit richly-valued cybersecurity names broadly.

MSTR.about: A business intelligence software company that has become best known for holding one of the largest corporate bitcoin treasuries in the world, making its stock trade heavily on bitcoin's price.
MSTR.performance: Strategy is down about 52% since the FY26 open, closely tracking the decline in bitcoin's price given how much of the company's balance sheet is held in the cryptocurrency.

FIG.about: A collaborative design and prototyping software company whose browser-based tools are widely used by product design teams.
FIG.performance: Figma is down about 55% since the FY26 open. As a recent IPO, the stock has seen a sharp valuation reset as post-listing enthusiasm faded and growth expectations normalized.

BYND.about: A maker of plant-based meat substitutes sold under its own brand through grocery and food-service channels.
BYND.performance: Beyond Meat is down about 78% since the FY26 open — the fund's worst performer by a wide margin. The company completed a 1-for-30 reverse stock split on August 14, 2026 as sales continued to decline and the plant-based meat category struggled broadly.

REVG.about: A specialty vehicle manufacturer building fire trucks, ambulances, RVs, and other emergency and specialty vehicles.
REVG.performance: REV Group merged into Terex Corporation on February 2, 2026 ($8.71 cash + 0.9809 Terex shares per REVG share). Valued at the current price of the combined company, the position is up about 15% since the FY26 open.

BITF.about: Originally a bitcoin mining company, Bitfarms completed a U.S. redomiciliation and rebranded to Keel Infrastructure Corp. in April 2026, pivoting toward high-performance computing and AI data-center hosting alongside its existing mining operations.
BITF.performance: Now trading as KEEL after a 1:1 rebrand, the position is up about 79% since the FY26 open — bitcoin-mining infrastructure stocks have rallied as the sector's AI/HPC pivot has drawn renewed investor interest.
